messages:
maria: heads-up — after yesterday's key rotation the ingest lambda started failing with AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt. stack trace shows assumed-role ARN.

maria: Error snippet: 
AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef12-3456

sam: did you confirm the lambda is assuming the new role/role session name? sometimes session policy strips kms perms.

maria: yes it's the same role. we rotate keys every 30d, this is the first time decrypt started failing right after rotation.

jin: two quick suspects: 1) key policy not allowing the assumed-role/principal (instead only allows the IAM user/role ARN), 2) grant token timing if a grant was used during rotation. also check for session policies or session tags blocking kms:Decrypt.

maria: how do I check the grant token situation? we didn't explicitly create a grant during rotation AFAIK.

sec-bot: cloudtrail event found: 
{ eventTime: "2026-01-12T17:02:03Z", eventName: "Decrypt", userIdentity: { type: "AssumedRole", arn: "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session" }, errorCode: "AccessDenied" }

alex: paste the key policy? often the key policy uses Principal with AWS: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root" and relies on IAM but if you locked it down during rotation it might not reference the new role ARNs.

maria: key policy excerpt: 
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowAccountRoot",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},
  "Action": "kms:*",
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

lucas: root allow alone should be fine if IAM policy grants kms:Decrypt to the role. but if the role is using an STS session policy (passed at assume-role) that denies kms:Decrypt, final decision is deny. check the assume-role call for a session policy param. also look at `aws:RequestedRegion` or `aws:CalledVia` conditions in key policy.

sam: run these to reproduce locally: 
```bash
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role --role-session-name debug-session --duration-seconds 900 > creds.json
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId creds.json)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(jq -r .Credentials.SecretAccessKey creds.json)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken creds.json)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc.blob --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef12-3456 --output text
```

maria: ran it, got same AccessDenied.

jin: then it's not the lambda environment. Next: check key policy for a Condition restricting by `aws:PrincipalArn` or `sts:SessionIssuer` fields. Also check service-linked condition `kms:EncryptionContext:aws:associated-service` if envelope encryption used.

alex: also check any grant objects on the key: `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` — if there was a grant created and used immediately, you might need to pass the grant token. but list-grants will show if grants exist and their granteePrincipal.

maria: list-grants returned empty. no grants.

lucas: then focus on policy + session. run `aws iam get-role --role-name ingest-role` and verify attached policies, then check STS assume-role call in the deploy script for `--policy` or `SessionPolicy` that could be removing kms permissions.

maria: found it — deploy script was adding a restrictive session policy when rotating credentials for the lambda invoker job. it was intended to limit S3 access but accidentally omitted kms:Decrypt in the permitted actions.

sam: nice catch. so fix options: 1) update rotation job to include kms:Decrypt in session policy, or 2) add explicit allow in key policy for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role` to bypass session policy restrictions (but note explicit Deny in session policy still wins).

maria: going to update rotation job to include kms:Decrypt + add a short-term key policy allow for the role while we rollout. cc @sec-bot for audit entry.

sec-bot: audit log created: ticket SEC-3421. Recorded change: rotation job session policy adjusted to include kms:Decrypt.

jin: one more note for future: prefer granting decrypt via resource-based key policy when possible for services that assume roles with session policies. session policy can't add permissions, only remove. resource policy can grant directly.

maria: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
